summary: Saxon con man Karl May invented a Wild West persona and wrote hugely popular Winnetou novels without visiting America; the books shaped Adolf Hitler's views on conquest, Lebensraum and the United States through World War II.

evidence.note: Karl May born in Saxony in 1842; childhood and early thefts follow
graduates 1860, jailed for a watch theft, then begins years of cons and prison
con career: fake doctor, fake policeman confiscating banknotes
1876 return home with invented travel past; first Winnetou novel 1893
1939 Poland invasion planning; Hitler blames generals for not reading May
May novels sent to officers fighting in Russia; Steiner detachment in 1945
Lebensraum framed via the American frontier and displacement of Native Americans
May's German-dominated America shapes Hitler's view of the US and the Bund
1908-1910 exposure of his past, US trip, death in 1912
legacy: 1960s Euro-westerns and present-day German Native American festivals

notes: Karl May and Hitler both treated as primary: May gets most airtime, but the title and pitch centre on Hitler's obsession, so nazism is the primary theme. Hitler's own life is not narrated birth to death; covered_span follows the lifetime rule. main_span runs from May's con career to 1945.
